questions.question: Does the unit follow naturally from the three-study overview and prepare the next section?
questions.answer: Yes. The overview separates three kinds of contribution. This unit then names required starting knowledge and shows each dependent route. Its closing instruction raises the distinction between reading a mechanism/result and checking a derivation, which the following section explains directly.

questions.question: Are the shorter place route and complete memory/eye route supported by the current teaching connections?
questions.answer: Yes. The two foundations teach rates, maps, shared variation and the difference between fixed spatial randomness and temporal motion. The place calculations use that background without the memory readout derivation. The memory/eye sequence needs its earlier diffusion and information development before circuit scaling.

questions.question: Can a first conceptual reading skip longer calculations without losing the needed explanation?
questions.answer: The current group readings support that scope: main text retains physical meanings, model assumptions and needed outcomes. Formal notes remain necessary to check full calculations. The next section explicitly states this distinction; the promise is not that every proof remains visible with folds closed.
